steps.why: A program asks for local stream sockets when it links, -ldolly-sockets, and then records sockets@0; test/fixtures/sockets.c names what each mode proves.
A pair inherited through spawn carries bytes both ways.
Network families, datagrams, abstract names and descriptor passing are refused by name.
A peer that exits or is killed is end of file to a waiting reader and EPIPE to a writer.
SIGPIPE ends a writer whose peer is gone, unless it is ignored.
Two programs the shell starts, sharing no pipe, meet at a path.
The server leaves its path behind: a dead listener refuses connections.
One process can take every socket the kernel holds; exit, a trap (its Worker fails) and forced termination of a CPU loop each give them back.
